_comment: css-backgrounds-3 §5.2 'Overlapping curves'. When the two radii on any side sum to more than that side's length, the correct behaviour is NOT to clamp that side's corners: compute f = min over all four sides of (side length / sum of its two radii), and if f < 1 multiply ALL EIGHT radii by f. The rule is global, so one oversized corner shrinks the other three. This is the behaviour, not the property, that is missing from the gating corpus: fixtures/visual-test.json declares radii on 20 components and every one of them is uniform (10/50/9999px, 25%/50%) or symmetric (20/0/20/0 on an unconstrained box), and uniform radii are the exact case where global scaling and naive per-corner clamping agree. Compose RoundedCornerShape, SwiftUI RoundedRectangle and DOM border-radius are three separate implementations of this rule, so it is a prime divergence candidate. Boxes are solid #9b59b6 on the #1A1A2E canvas; no text, no borders, no padding, so the only variable per row is the radius declaration. Each _note gives the spec radii AND what a per-corner clamp would produce instead, so a reviewer can read the answer off the capture rather than eyeball it. Rows 1-2 are controls that pin f; rows 3, 4 and 6 are the discriminators.

BRS_NoOverlap_Control._note: CONTROL. 200x100, r=20 everywhere. Side sums are 40 <= 200 and 40 <= 100, so f = 1 and no scaling happens. EXPECTED: uniform 20px corners; each corner sheds 400 - 100*pi = 85.84 px to the canvas colour.

BRS_UniformOverlap_Scaled._note: CONTROL that pins f. 200x40, r=40 everywhere. f = min(200/80, 40/80, 200/80, 40/80) = 0.5, so every radius becomes 20px. EXPECTED: uniform 20px corners on a 200x40 box — NOT a 40px pill. This row deliberately does not discriminate: per-corner clamping to half the shorter side also gives 20. It is here so that a failure in the next rows cannot be blamed on f itself.

BRS_Asymmetric_LargeTopLeft._note: DISCRIMINATOR. 200x40, border-radius: 40px 8px 8px 8px (TL TR BR BL). Sides: top 48 <= 200 (4.17), right 16 <= 40 (2.5), bottom 16 <= 200 (12.5), left 40/48 = 0.8333 — the left side binds. f = 0.8333 scales EVERY corner: TL 33.33px, TR = BR = BL 6.67px. EXPECTED per spec: one large corner near 33px and three near 6.7px. A PER-CORNER CLAMP instead gives TL = min(40, 20) = 20 and the other three an unshrunk 8 — wrong at all four corners, and wrong in opposite directions, so it cannot be mistaken for antialiasing.

BRS_Asymmetric_OppositeCorners._note: DISCRIMINATOR, opposite direction — here the spec answer is BIGGER than the naive one. 120x60, border-radius: 50px 0 50px 0. Because the two large radii sit on OPPOSITE corners, no side sums past its length: top 50 <= 120, right 50 <= 60, bottom 50 <= 120, left 50 <= 60. f = 1. EXPECTED: full 50px curves at top-left and bottom-right, square top-right and bottom-left. A platform that clamps every radius to min(width, height)/2 = 30 shrinks both curves by 20px and fails here while passing every uniform fixture in the repo.

BRS_Percent_Ellipse._note: §5.1 percentage resolution: the HORIZONTAL radius resolves against the border-box width, the VERTICAL against its height. 100x40 at 50% gives every corner 50px horizontal by 20px vertical; side sums are exactly 100 <= 100 and 40 <= 40, so f = 1. EXPECTED: a true 100x40 ELLIPSE, area pi*50*20 = 3141.6 px, leaving 858.4 px of canvas at the corners. A platform that resolves both axes against one dimension collapses to 20px round corners on a rectangle (3656.6 px of fill) — a 515 px difference. The gating corpus only ever puts 50% on a square (Avatar_Circle 80x80) or 25% on 120x80, so neither ratio is extreme enough to separate these.

BRS_Asymmetric_DominantCorner._note: DISCRIMINATOR on a square box, so no aspect-ratio explanation is available. 100x100, border-radius: 90px 20px 20px 20px. Top and left both sum to 110 > 100, giving f = 100/110 = 0.909: TL 81.82px, the other three 18.18px. EXPECTED: one very large corner just over 80px and three just over 18px. A per-corner clamp gives TL = min(90, 50) = 50 and the others an unshrunk 20 — a 32px error on the dominant corner.
